subject: [Invite] SF dinner with Rivian, 1X, Dexterity, BotCo, and Genesis AI
text:
Hi [NAME],

We're hosting a private AI leaders dinner next Thursday (30 Oct,
6:30-9:30pm) at Spruce in SF with Founders and Heads of AI joining us from
Rivian, 1X, Dexterity, BotCo, and Genesis AI.

Arne Stoschek joined our last dinner in Palo Alto - I assume you know him
from your Acubed days - and we'd love for you to join us this time.

It's a small group (~25 guests) hosted by our Co-Founder, [SENDER], focused on
the multimodal shift in AI; how vision is converging with language,
robotics, and embodied systems.

For context, Encord is fast becoming the de facto ML data layer for many
physical AI companies (Boston Dynamics, Figure AI, Woven by Toyota,
Thinking Machine Labs and more) to help unify 2D and 3D sensor fusion
pipelines. We're big fans of [COMPANY], so would be great to connect in person.

Would you be up for joining? I can send over the full invite.

subject: SF in-person connect
text:
Hi [NAME],

We've not been introduced yet, but Vivek Nayak came to our AI leaders
dinner we hosted in Seattle back in May, so we caught with him there and
afterwards.

I'm flying over to SF (from London) next week for two weeks, and noticed
you're based in the Bay Area. Would be keen to grab a coffee if you're
interested and around from the 27th of Oct - 5th of Nov?

Vivek mentioned it's still too early to consider partnering with Encord,
but I'm keen to hear more about your work regardless. Can share more about
what we're seeing in the robotics space more widely.

Let me know if you're around and interested, and we can schedule something.

Look forward to it.

subject: partner - [COMPANY]
text:
Hi [NAME],

Saw you are building smart alerts at [COMPANY] - sounds like you're developing
in-house vision models.

A lot of the surveillance teams we work with (LiveView Tech, Voxel, Flock
Safety) hit similar scaling challenges when open-source tools can't keep up
with large volumes of video data or complex edge cases like weather noise
or mask wearing intruders.

Encord helps them improve data quality at scale with model-assisted
pre-labeling, native video annotation, automated QA workflow, HITL review
and model evaluation. So teams can focus on fine tuning models and less
wrangling data bottlenecks.

Would love to show how this might fit your current setup - open for a quick
chat Tuesdays to Fridays morning PT?

subject: [NAME] - E-MM1
text:
Hi [NAME],

Hopefully you've received an access link to E-MM1. I imagine you are using
multiple modalities to develop vision models at Streetscope - you might
find our customer retrieval model relevant for training/fine tuning your
models.

We've been working on projects w/ Nexar, Motive, Motive, and Woven
(Toyota), etc. developing models for road safety and driver safety for
collison prevision use cases. Seems like it's pretty similar to what you're
building at Streetscope.

Quick context: Encord is a data layer scale-up ($50M Series B), providing
native video annotation, model-assisted pre-labeling, automated QA
workflows - aimed at improving training data quality at scale - something
open source tooling struggles with.

Happy to share more if you're interested to know what your peers' been up
to - I'm flexible Tuesday to Friday mornings PT.

subject: [Invite] Encord AI Leaders Dinner @ Spruce, SF - Oct 30th
text:
Hi [NAME],

We're hosting a private AI leaders dinner next Thursday (30 Oct,
6:30-9:30pm) at Spruce in SF with Founders and AI Leaders from Thinking
Machine Labs, Genesis AI, Rime AI, Higgsfield, Cartesia, Twelve Labs and
more. We'd love for you to join us!

It's a small group (~25 guests) hosted by our Co-Founder, [SENDER], focused on
the multimodal shift in AI; how vision is converging with language,
robotics, and embodied systems. Would be great to have yours and Otter's
voice in the room.

For context, Encord is a multimodal (audio, text, image, video) ML DataOps
platform that unifies data curation, annotation and model eval in one
platform. We help Udio, Thinking Machine Labs, Eleven Labs and more tackle
challenges around manual & auto-annotation, evaluation, and scalable
pipelines.

Would you be up for joining? I can send over the full invite.
